sections.title: Overview
content: This document captures our findings, limitations, and recommendations regarding WordPress.com's GitHub Deployments feature. The information is based on practical testing conducted during the cFish.io project in March 2025.

sections.title: What Is GitHub Deployments for WordPress.com?
content: GitHub Deployments is a feature available on WordPress.com Business plans that allows automatic deployment of code changes from a GitHub repository to a WordPress.com site. In theory, this enables a modern development workflow where code can be version-controlled and collaboratively developed before being deployed to production.

sections.title: Testing Methodology
content: - Setting up a GitHub repository with WordPress theme files
- Creating both parent theme modifications and child theme customizations
- Attempting various types of theme customizations

content.subtitle: 1. Parent Theme Protection
items: WordPress.com appears to prevent modifications to parent themes entirely
Changes made to parent theme files (e.g., header.html, footer.html) are not deployed
This protection likely exists to ensure theme updates can be safely applied

content.subtitle: 2. Child Theme Requirements
items: Child themes must follow strict formatting requirements
Must include properly formatted style.css with Template: declaration
GitHub Theme URI must exactly match the repository owner/name format
Complete theme structure is necessary even for small customizations

content.subtitle: 3. Selective Deployment
items: Not all pushed files are deployed to the live site
Some file types or locations may be ignored or filtered
Deployment logs show successful processing but changes don't always appear

content.subtitle: 4. Block Editor Incompatibility
items: Sites built with WordPress.com's block editor don't map 1:1 to theme files
Block-based customizations made in WordPress.com admin may override theme files
Traditional theme development patterns may conflict with block editor structures

content.subtitle: 5. Limited Documentation
items: Official documentation lacks details on specific limitations
No clear guidance on best practices for theme development with GitHub Deployments
Error handling and troubleshooting information is minimal

content.subtitle: What Works:
items: Simple child theme structures with proper metadata
CSS customizations within child themes
Template overrides following WordPress hierarchy
Adding new templates or parts to child themes

content.subtitle: What Doesn't Work:
items: Direct parent theme modifications
Inconsistent or incomplete child theme structures
Complex theme frameworks or non-standard patterns
Attempts to override WordPress.com's core functionality

content.subtitle: Development Workflow
items: 1. **Start With Local Environment**
Build the site completely in a local environment first
Use standard WordPress development tools and patterns
Test thoroughly before attempting deployment 2. **Follow WordPress Standards**
Use proper child theme structure for all customizations
Follow template hierarchy for overrides
Maintain proper theme metadata 3. **Deployment Strategy**
Consider alternatives to WordPress.com if extensive customization is needed
Use WordPress.com primarily for content and basic layout
Utilize GitHub Deployments mainly for child themes and plugins 4. **Testing Process**
Create a staging site for initial deployment testing
Document exactly what changes are deployable
Maintain separate workflows for theme vs. content changes

content.subtitle: Alternatives to Consider
items: Self-hosted WordPress with direct GitHub integration
WordPress hosting providers with more flexible deployment options
Headless WordPress setups for more development flexibility

sections.title: Conclusion
content: WordPress.com's GitHub Deployments feature provides basic integration between GitHub repositories and WordPress.com sites. However, its limitations make it most suitable for simple customizations rather than extensive theme development. For projects requiring significant custom development, alternative hosting solutions may provide more flexibility and control.
